newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan bank lending falls in November - BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Japan bank lending falls in November - BOJ.

text.p: Daily aggregate outstanding lending by Japan's 149 banks in November dipped 0.5 percent from a year earlier to 526.08 trillion yen, the second year-on-year decline in a row, the Bank of Japan (BOJ) said on Wednesday.

The average total lending balance of Japan's 10 big commercial banks was 242.34 trillion yen in November, down 0.1 percent from a year earlier, which was the first decline in 17 months, the BOJ said in a statement.
The average total lending balance of three long-term credit banks fell 4.1 percent to 44.9 trillion yen and that of seven major trust banks dropped 4.2 percent to 53.56 trillion yen.
The average total lending balance of 64 regional banks, meanwhile, grew 1.9 percent to 133.35 trillion yen, while that at 65 second-tier regional banks fell 1.5 percent to 51.93 trillion yen.
